data.gender_notes: Shalabh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Sanskrit word शलभ (śalabha), which means 'one who conquers'. It is a powerful name that resonates with strength, courage, and the ability to overcome challenges. The name Shalabh carries the meaning “One who conquers” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Shalabh usually hope their child will grow to embody one who conquers and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Shalabh is a reminder of the inner strength and courage that resides within each of us. It encourages us to face our fears and challenges with determination and resilience, and to trust in our ability to overcome any obstacle.
data.etymology: Shalabh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who conquers.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shalabh total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shalabh holds significant cultural importance in Hindu mythology, particularly in the context of the Mahabharata. Shalabh is the name of one of the Panchala king's sons, Vibhishana, who later becomes a key ally of Lord Rama during his exile and eventual battle against the demon King Ravana to rescue his wife Sita. The name symbolizes courage, loyalty, and wisdom, which are important values in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: At a deeper spiritual level, the name Shalabh can be understood as a reminder of one's inner strength and ability to overcome challenges. It encourages individuals to tap into their inner resources and face adversity with courage and resilience. The name also embodies the concept of Shakti or power within, reminding us that each one of us has the potential to conquer our weaknesses and inner demons. By embracing the name Shalabh, one can affirm their commitment to spiritual growth and personal development.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shalabh is a name of Vayu Dev (Wind God). It symbolizes the swift and powerful movement of the wind, carrying the essence of life and change. It is a reminder of the transient nature of life and the importance of adaptability and flexibility.

historical_references.reference: Shalabh was a king mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, who ruled the kingdom of Madra. He was a powerful warrior and a friend of the Pandava brothers.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Hindu mythology and literature

historical_references.reference: Shalabh is also mentioned in Jain texts as a ruler of the Anavattha region. He is known for his patronage of Jain monks and his role in the spread of Jainism during the 6th century BCE.
